section_summary: This section contains State Department, embassy, and FBI correspondence on Japanese residents and organizations in Peru, chiefly from 1945. The enclosed reports examine commercial ties, community leadership, propaganda allegations, and possible espionage, often finding no evidence of current subversive activity. The final two documents, from 1946, concern rumors that Japan had not lost the war and a reported secret organization spreading that claim.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on people in Nobuo Yatoh’s address book
subfiles.about: Transmits a report on sixteen people whose Peruvian addresses appeared in Nobuo Yatoh’s address book.
subfiles.summary: Forwards an FBI source report on Yatoh’s Peruvian contacts.

subfiles.title: Report on Peruvian contacts in Nobuo Yatoh’s address book
subfiles.about: Reviews the identities, businesses, movements, and possible political activity of people named in Yatoh’s address book.
subfiles.summary: The surviving report begins mid-discussion and profiles Japanese residents and other contacts in Peru, including merchants, former company officers, and members of community associations. It compares confidential-source accounts with commercial and alien-registration records, noting deportations, Proclaimed List entries, and occasional conflicting claims. For several subjects it finds no evidence of current activity against the Allies.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Juan Barthelmes
subfiles.about: Forwards information that Barthelmes may still represent Japanese commercial interests in Peru.
subfiles.summary: Flags a possible purchasing link between blacklisted Japanese firms and Ezra Chrem & Company.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Juan Barthelmes
subfiles.about: Reports Barthelmes’s business connections, property, and suspected intermediary role for blacklisted Japanese firms.
subfiles.summary: Sources describe Barthelmes’s ties to Taibo, the Chrem firms, and attorney Carlos Basurto.

subfiles.title: Instruction concerning The Japanese in Peru manuscript
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Lima
subfiles.about: Requests the Peruvian Foreign Office’s decision and embassy comments on John K. Emmerson’s manuscript.
subfiles.summary: Asks whether Peru has completed its review of The Japanese in Peru.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Sakuichi Wakao
subfiles.about: Forwards a report on Wakao, an internment-related letter, and Japanese propaganda films.
subfiles.summary: Introduces allegations involving Wakao’s circulated letter and film distribution.

subfiles.title: Report on Sakuichi Wakao
subfiles.about: Investigates allegations that Wakao spread claims about Japanese internees and helped exhibit Japanese propaganda films.
subfiles.summary: The report tests a claim that Wakao circulated a letter alleging mistreatment of Japanese internees in the United States; an account of the letter’s delivery is disputed. It documents his blacklisted bazaar, Japanese community offices, and prewar film activity with Itsuke Tanabe. Surveillance disclosed no unusual current activity.

subfiles.title: Embassy despatch on publication of The Japanese in Peru
subfiles.about: Reports Peru’s preference that Emmerson’s manuscript remain unpublished until after its elections.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office suggests reconsideration after elections, possibly with textual changes.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Manuel Fusumada
subfiles.about: Forwards an investigation of Manuel Fusumada’s background and present livelihood.
subfiles.summary: Reports that Fusumada now earns money selling novelties.

subfiles.title: Report on Manuel Yoshiro Fusumada
subfiles.about: Reviews Fusumada’s community leadership, employment, financial decline, and alien-registration record.
subfiles.summary: An anonymous accusation prompted inquiries into Fusumada, a former Japanese society president and interpreter. Sources describe bankruptcy, later sales work, and a modest present income.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Hyochichi Sato
subfiles.about: Forwards a report on a photographer formerly associated with the Japanese colony and legation.
subfiles.summary: States that no evidence of current subversive activity was developed.

subfiles.title: Report on Hyochichi Sato
subfiles.about: Examines allegations of pro-Japanese meetings at Sato’s photography studio.
subfiles.summary: Sources describe Sato’s travel, studio, Japanese clientele, and nephew Kiyoshi’s management. The report records family and registration details without establishing subversive activity.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Riyoko Kiyohiro
subfiles.about: Forwards information on a former Japanese Legation employee now operating a pastry shop.
subfiles.summary: Reports no indication of current subversive activity.

subfiles.title: Report on Riyoko Kiyohiro and aliases
subfiles.about: Investigates Kiyohiro’s newspaper and legation work, travel to Japan, and Callao pastry business.
subfiles.summary: The report reconciles Kiyohiro’s aliases and alien-registration records with accounts of his employment and business. Sources characterize the pastry shop as modest, and police and surveillance sources report no evidence of current subversive activity.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Yoshiyuki Tamura
subfiles.about: Forwards a report on Tamura’s newspaper work, Japan trip, and Domei Press connection.
subfiles.summary: Introduces confidential-source information on Yoshiyuki Tamura.

subfiles.title: Report on Yoshiyuki Tamura
subfiles.about: Examines Tamura’s prewar press career and his management of Japanese interests through the Spanish Embassy.
subfiles.summary: The report traces Tamura’s Japanese newspaper and Domei Press work, then describes how he succeeded a deported community adviser. It details Spanish Embassy handling of pensions, registration, remittances, disputes, and deportees’ property, with Tamura portrayed as a principal intermediary. Sources also discuss his associates and the effect of the Spanish Embassy’s withdrawal from Japanese representation.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Keisaburo Sato
subfiles.about: Forwards a report on a former Huaral Japanese society president.
subfiles.summary: Notes no indication that Sato engaged in espionage or subversive activity.

subfiles.title: Report on Keisaburo Sato
subfiles.about: Investigates Sato’s society office, farming history, finances, and current employment.
subfiles.summary: Sources describe a former Japanese society president whose Chancay Valley farming ended after he lost access to land. He moved to Lima and took work in a public-health work camp; no espionage or subversive activity is indicated.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Takeo Kikkawa
subfiles.about: Forwards information on Kikkawa’s leadership among Japanese residents in Chiclayo.
subfiles.summary: Reports no indication of current espionage or subversive activity.

subfiles.title: Report on Takeo Kikkawa
subfiles.about: Reviews Kikkawa’s association with deported Chiclayo leader Usaburo Maoki and his work history.
subfiles.summary: Kikkawa reportedly assumed local leadership; sources now describe him raising chickens without evidence of subversive activity.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Pedro Kichinosuke Yoshimoto
subfiles.about: Forwards a report on Yoshimoto’s Lima property and political contacts.
subfiles.summary: States that investigation found no recent subversive activity.

subfiles.title: Report on Pedro Kichinosuke Yoshimoto
subfiles.about: Examines Yoshimoto’s dairy, rental properties, alleged political influence, and Proclaimed List entry.
subfiles.summary: Sources portray Yoshimoto as a substantial property owner with political contacts, while an auction notice records seizure of his dairy. They report no current subversive activity.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Yukio Yoshioka
subfiles.about: Forwards information on a Japanese merchant and former society treasurer.
subfiles.summary: Notes liquidation of Yoshioka’s business and no known current subversive activity.

subfiles.title: Report on Yukio Yoshioka
subfiles.about: Details Yoshioka’s import firm, Japanese commercial associations, community offices, and present circumstances.
subfiles.summary: Sources describe Yoshioka’s rise as an importer, his leadership in Japanese commercial and community organizations, and the government liquidation of his firm in 1942. The report records his business associates, family, travel, and registration details. Sources know of no present activity harmful to the Allies.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Yoshiyuki Tamura at the Swedish Legation
subfiles.about: Forwards a follow-up report on Tamura’s work in the Swedish Legation’s Japanese section.
subfiles.summary: Introduces updated information on Tamura’s diplomatic work.

subfiles.title: Follow-up memorandum on Yoshiyuki Tamura
subfiles.about: Reports the transfer of Japanese-interest files and staff from the Spanish Embassy to the Swedish Legation.
subfiles.summary: Tamura and Luis Okamoto work in the Swedish Legation’s Japanese section; sources report no current subversive activity.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Japanese instructor Bunei Nakada, first copy
subfiles.about: Forwards an inquiry into Nakada’s Japanese-language teaching in Lima.
subfiles.summary: Reports private instruction and no apparent current subversive activity.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Japanese instructor Bunei Nakada, second copy
subfiles.about: Repeats the FBI transmittal concerning Nakada’s Japanese-language instruction.
subfiles.summary: Second copy of the August 7 transmittal.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Bunei Nakada’s language lessons
subfiles.about: Describes Nakada’s selective home instruction in Japanese reading and writing.
subfiles.summary: Nakada teaches children in their homes; the source finds no subversive use of the lessons.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Fumizo Iki
subfiles.about: Forwards information on a longtime Japanese resident associated with the Chancay Valley society.
subfiles.summary: Notes no indication of current subversive activity.

subfiles.title: Report on Fumizo Iki, also known as Fumizo Ito
subfiles.about: Traces Iki’s farm work, financial decline, and disputed claim to Japanese society leadership.
subfiles.summary: A source disputes that Iki led the society and reports no espionage or subversive activity.

subfiles.title: Embassy despatch on rumors that Japan had not lost the war
subfiles.about: Relays an informant’s account of false victory rumors in Lima’s Japanese colony.
subfiles.summary: Rumors portray MacArthur as a prisoner; the embassy has not obtained the letters said to spread them.

subfiles.title: FBI letter on Aikoku Doshi Kay
subfiles.about: Reports a purported secret Japanese group in Lima claiming that the war continues.
subfiles.summary: An alleged former officer from Brazil reportedly recruits members and raises funds while spreading claims that Japan is still fighting.
